Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and throughput for an AI customer-facing chat product. Key ask: contractual latency SLOs with clear measurement source and test harness.

- Customer wants SLOs defined as p50/p95/p99 for both request-complete (non-streaming) and per-token streaming latency.
- They insist on client-side (browser/edge) E2E timings for commercial SLA, but are open to hybrid: Redwood gateway metrics for ops + client-side probes for contractual measurement.
- SE notes: important to align on what the p95 includes — network + gateway + server compute + first-byte vs last-byte. Customer wording: "we measure what our users see".
- POC details: running a 48h soak with reserved 8xA100 equivalent capacity, synthetic concurrency profile mimicking peak concurrent users 350 with average 120 tokens per request.
- Measurement instrumentation: recommend dual reporting — Prometheus histograms aggregated at service ingress (server-side) and synthetic Puppeteer-based client probes (client-side). Use consistent percentile aggregation window (60s sliding) in contract.
- Tail mitigation discussed: prefix/KV cache for hot prompts, automatic reroute to warm reserve, token-batching knobs in Optimize. Expect ~20-30% p95 improvement with KV caching on common prefixes.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask is 8 GPUs with policy for 40% burst to shared pool. SE estimate: for their model (7B MQA) 1 GPU ~ 45 qps non-streaming baseline; need 6-9 GPUs depending on targeted p95 SLA.
- SLA negotiation points: credit formula for p99 violations (per-minute contract vs per-day aggregate), measurement source (client vs gateway), and emergency fallback routing.
- Outstanding: legal wants explicit definition for streaming p99 (is it per-token tail or per-request time to final token?). Avoid ambiguous language.
